duties.remaining: Still not written from pp. 38-39: (1) the remark that adjoining quantifiers from partially ordered prefixes gives the full expressive power of second-order logic is reported as Ebbinghaus's remark, not stated as a theorem; its precise form from Ch. VI Section 1 (Mundici Theorem 1.1.2) is linked as thm:p03-w03-p03-042-mundici-pc-ec, owned by w03-p03-042. (2) Many-sorted vocabularies: Ebbinghaus formulates the relativization and substitution properties only in the one-sorted case (Ch. II, p. 30) and gives the Q^H clause for one universe (p. 38); the one-sorted regularity theorem covers the claim as these definitions state it, and the Definition 1.2.1 properties for a many-sorted Q^H are not written because no many-sorted Q^H clause is in the pages read. Former item (3) is closed: the substitution property for every symbol holds when only finitely many function symbols and constants are replaced, and thm:p03-w03-p03-044-substitution-limit proves that it fails, for L(Q^H) and for first-order logic, with infinitely many replaced constants.
